What the literature establishes: Indirect injection is demonstrated, benchmarked and adaptive; defenses of the time were bypassed
What is uncertain: Magnitude: 24% to 84.30% average ASR across benchmarks
What is under-evaluated: Tool-metadata, tool-library, skill and MCP-server threats against runtime defenses
Implication for REM: Focus on indirect injection; state other classes as out of scope

What the literature establishes: The observation channel (tool outputs, retrieved content, tool metadata) is the decisive entry for tool-using agents
What is uncertain: Relative danger of channels (skills > email/web in one study)
Implication for REM: Mediate at the action, where all channels converge

What the literature establishes: Input, call, plan, data-flow and trajectory units all implemented
What is uncertain: Which unit gives the best security–utility trade-off
What is under-evaluated: Head-to-head comparisons on a shared workload
Implication for REM: Per-call observation with provenance context is a defensible, not novel, choice

What the literature establishes: Interception at the tool boundary is widespread (41/42 runtime; 34/42 tool/action) and fast
What is under-evaluated: Evaluation on benchmarks the authors did not build
What differs across studies: Permission vs. alignment vs. provenance vs. harm

What the literature establishes: Many monitors model sequences (17/42 behavioral; 21/42 multi-step)
What is under-evaluated: Contribution inside a probabilistic estimator; financial settings
What differs across studies: Automata, Markov chains, latent states, heuristics
Implication for REM: Measure and report the contribution; do not assume it

What the literature establishes: Informative against injected or misaligned calls; cross-step labels had a 26.4-point effect in one study
What is uncertain: Whether the effect generalizes beyond the authors' datasets
What is under-evaluated: Provenance as input to a calibrated estimator; financial arguments
What differs across studies: Obtained by analysis, construction or labels
Implication for REM: Use as estimator input; test the contribution

What the literature establishes: Logistic scoring, calibration, expected cost, reject option and attribution are established; one agent-safety precedent (NEXUS)
What is uncertain: Behaviour in combination at the action boundary
What is under-evaluated: Calibration of agent-safety probabilities; calibration vs. control
Implication for REM: Adopted methods; report calibration separately from control

What the literature establishes: Graduated responses and consequence information are common
What is uncertain: How to combine an induction probability with a declared consequence
What differs across studies: Fixed costs, pricing, rules, judge dimensions
Implication for REM: Test the combination against a same-estimator consequence-independent baseline

What the literature establishes: Block, modify, escalate, restrict, roll back and undo all implemented
What is uncertain: Effectiveness of each response once chosen
What differs across studies: Meaning of "escalate" (human vs. stronger judge) and "modify"
Implication for REM: Report residual attack success and escalation rate; SC-1 and SC-2 remain open

What the literature establishes: Financial actions lie within general benchmarks' attack surface; one financial harness exists
What is under-evaluated: Every financial-context study is LIMITED EVIDENCE; key figures were measured on a benchmark withdrawn for non-scientific reasons and cannot be confirmed
What differs across studies: Chatbot firewall, position paper, actuarial framework, judge harness
Implication for REM: Report results per financial action type and consequence tier

What the literature establishes: Results are benchmark-specific; many benchmarks are built with the defense they evaluate
What is under-evaluated: Independent evaluation; decomposition into security, utility, intervention, calibration and latency
Implication for REM: Per-benchmark reporting with benign utility, intervention rates, calibration and latency
